title: Parameters, arguments, return types and void
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C language rules.
Trace the example and explain data flow.
Identify common errors and boundary conditions.
Apply the concept in a small tested program.

understand.concept: Parameters are named objects declared in a function's parameter list; arguments are the expressions supplied at a call. A return type describes the value produced by a function. void as a parameter list in a declaration means the function takes no arguments; void as a return type means it returns no value.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct function interfaces make data flow explicit and help the compiler diagnose incompatible calls.
understand.analogy: Treat a function or pointer operation as an explicit contract between caller and callee.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal rules for types, object lifetime, scope and linkage.

explain.narrative:
Parameters are named objects declared in a function's parameter list; arguments are the expressions supplied at a call. A return type describes the value produced by a function. void as a parameter list in a declaration means the function takes no arguments; void as a return type means it returns no value.

When applying this concept, check declared types, preconditions, object lifetime and all control-flow paths. Compile with warnings enabled and test both typical and boundary inputs.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: get_default_count takes no arguments and returns an int. Its result becomes the argument passed to show_total, which returns no value.

practise.guidedTask: Identify each parameter, argument, return type and void use.
practise.independentTask: Declare and define one function that accepts no arguments and returns a status code, plus one function that accepts a value and prints it.
hints: In a prototype, f(void) explicitly declares no parameters in C.
A function returning void must not be used where a value is required.
Match format specifiers to the actual argument types.
